The [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics"), officially known as the Games of the XXX Olympiad, was a summer [multi-sport event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-sport_event "Multi-sport event") held in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), the capital of the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), from 27 July to 12 August. A total of 10,768 athletes from 204 nations participated in 302 medal events in 26 sports across 39 different disciplines.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-Facts_and_Figures-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-2)

Overall, 86 nations received at least one medal, and 55 of them won at least one gold medal. Athletes from the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "United States at the 2012 Summer Olympics") won the most medals overall, with 105, and the most gold medals, with 48.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-3)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-CBS-4) The latter record is the largest gold medal haul for the country at a non-US-hosted Olympics.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-CBS-4) Host nation [Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Britain_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Great Britain at the 2012 Summer Olympics")[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-TeamGB-6) won 29 gold medals and 65 overall medals, making it the most successful Olympics performance for that nation since the [1908 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1908_Summer_Olympics "1908 Summer Olympics").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-7)

[Michael Phelps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Phelps "Michael Phelps") and [Missy Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missy_Franklin "Missy Franklin") won the most gold medals at the Games with four each. Phelps also won the highest number of medals overall, winning six in total.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-8)[Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrain_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Bahrain at the 2012 Summer Olympics"),[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-Bahrain-10)[Botswana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botswana_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Botswana at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Cyprus at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), [Gabon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabon_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Gabon at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), [Grenada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenada_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Grenada at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), [Guatemala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Guatemala at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), and [Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montenegro_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Montenegro at the 2012 Summer Olympics") all won their first Olympic medals, with Bahrain and Grenada as well as Serbia winning their nation's first Olympic gold medal.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-Facts_and_Figures-1) Previously, Montenegrin athletes had competed as nationals of [Serbia and Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia_and_Montenegro_at_the_Olympics "Serbia and Montenegro at the Olympics") and of [Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslavia_at_the_Olympics "Yugoslavia at the Olympics").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-Montenegro-11)[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-IndieAhtletes-12) Taekwondo athlete [Milica Mandić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milica_Mandi%C4%87 "Milica Mandić") from [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Serbia at the 2012 Summer Olympics") won the first Olympic gold medal as an independent nation.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-13)

During and after the Games, many athletes who were caught doping, or tested positive for banned substances, were disqualified from competition and had their medals revoked.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-SI_Russia_Doping-14)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-15) To date, 43 [medals have been stripped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stripped_Olympic_medals "List of stripped Olympic medals"), with [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Russia at the 2012 Summer Olympics") accounting for 20 of those.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-16)

The medal table is based on information provided by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) and is consistent with IOC convention in its published medal tables. The table uses the [Olympic medal table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_medal_table "Olympic medal table") sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a [National Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") (NOC). The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next, and then the number of bronze medals.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-24)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-25) If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [IOC country code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_IOC_country_codes "List of IOC country codes").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-26)

On 29 August 2016, a report indicated that a retested sample for [Besik Kudukhov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Besik_Kudukhov "Besik Kudukhov") of Russia, the silver medallist in the [men's 60 kg freestyle wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_freestyle_60_kg "Wrestling at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's freestyle 60 kg") event, had returned a positive result (later disclosed as [dehydrochlormethyltestosterone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehydrochlormethyltestosterone "Dehydrochlormethyltestosterone")).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-36) Kudukhov died in a car crash in December 2013. On 27 October 2016, the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) dropped all disciplinary proceedings against Kudukhov, stating that such proceedings cannot be conducted against a deceased person.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-37)

The [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics"), officially known as the Games of the XXX Olympiad, was a summer [multi-sport event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-sport_event "Multi-sport event") held in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), the capital of the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), from 27 July to 12 August. A total of 10,768 athletes from 204 nations participated in 302 medal events in 26 sports across 39 different disciplines.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-Facts_and_Figures-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-2)

Overall, 86 nations received at least one medal, and 55 of them won at least one gold medal. Athletes from the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "United States at the 2012 Summer Olympics") won the most medals overall, with 105, and the most gold medals, with 48.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-3)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-CBS-4) The latter record is the largest gold medal haul for the country at a non-US-hosted Olympics.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-CBS-4) Host nation [Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Britain_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Great Britain at the 2012 Summer Olympics")[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-TeamGB-6) won 29 gold medals and 65 overall medals, making it the most successful Olympics performance for that nation since the [1908 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1908_Summer_Olympics "1908 Summer Olympics").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-7)

[Michael Phelps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Phelps "Michael Phelps") and [Missy Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missy_Franklin "Missy Franklin") won the most gold medals at the Games with four each. Phelps also won the highest number of medals overall, winning six in total.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-8)[Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrain_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Bahrain at the 2012 Summer Olympics"),[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-Bahrain-10)[Botswana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botswana_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Botswana at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Cyprus at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), [Gabon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabon_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Gabon at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), [Grenada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenada_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Grenada at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), [Guatemala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Guatemala at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), and [Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montenegro_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Montenegro at the 2012 Summer Olympics") all won their first Olympic medals, with Bahrain and Grenada as well as Serbia winning their nation's first Olympic gold medal.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-Facts_and_Figures-1) Previously, Montenegrin athletes had competed as nationals of [Serbia and Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia_and_Montenegro_at_the_Olympics "Serbia and Montenegro at the Olympics") and of [Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslavia_at_the_Olympics "Yugoslavia at the Olympics").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-Montenegro-11)[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-IndieAhtletes-12) Taekwondo athlete [Milica Mandić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milica_Mandi%C4%87 "Milica Mandić") from [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Serbia at the 2012 Summer Olympics") won the first Olympic gold medal as an independent nation.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-13)

During and after the Games, many athletes who were caught doping, or tested positive for banned substances, were disqualified from competition and had their medals revoked.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-SI_Russia_Doping-14)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-15) To date, 43 [medals have been stripped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stripped_Olympic_medals "List of stripped Olympic medals"), with [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Russia at the 2012 Summer Olympics") accounting for 20 of those.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-16)

The medal table is based on information provided by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) and is consistent with IOC convention in its published medal tables. The table uses the [Olympic medal table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_medal_table "Olympic medal table") sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a [National Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") (NOC). The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next, and then the number of bronze medals.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-24)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-25) If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [IOC country code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_IOC_country_codes "List of IOC country codes").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-26)

In [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Boxing at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), [judo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judo_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Judo at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Taekwondo at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), and [wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Wrestling at the 2012 Summer Olympics"), two bronze medals are awarded in each weight class.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-27)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-28)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-29)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-30) Two silver medals (and no bronze) were awarded for second-place ties in both the [men's 200 metre freestyle On 29 August 2016, a report indicated that a retested sample for [Besik Kudukhov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Besik_Kudukhov "Besik Kudukhov") of Russia, the silver medallist in the [men's 60 kg freestyle wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_freestyle_60_kg "Wrestling at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's freestyle 60 kg") event, had returned a positive result (later disclosed as [dehydrochlormethyltestosterone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehydrochlormethyltestosterone "Dehydrochlormethyltestosterone")).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-36) Kudukhov died in a car crash in December 2013. On 27 October 2016, the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) dropped all disciplinary proceedings against Kudukhov, stating that such proceedings cannot be conducted against a deceased person.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-37)

The [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics"), officially known as the Games of the XXXI Olympiad, and officially branded as Rio 2016, were an international [multi-sport event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-sport_event "Multi-sport event") held from 5 to 21 August 2016 in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), Brazil, with preliminary events in some sports beginning on 3 August.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-IOC_Rio_2016-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-4) 11,238 athletes representing 207 [National Olympic Committees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") (NOCs) participated, including first-time entrants [Kosovo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosovo_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Kosovo at the 2016 Summer Olympics"), [South Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "South Sudan at the 2016 Summer Olympics"), and the [Refugee Olympic Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugee_Olympic_Team_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Refugee Olympic Team at the 2016 Summer Olympics").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-IOC_Rio_2016-3) The games featured 306 medal events in 28 [sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_sports "Olympic sports") and 41 disciplines.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-IOC_Rio_2016-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-5) The 2016 Summer Games were the first Olympics to be held in [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-6)

Athletes representing 87 NOCs received at least one medal, breaking the record of most NOCs winning a medal at a single edition of the Olympics.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-7)[[A]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-12) Athletes from 59 nations ## Medals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Medals")]

See also: [Olympic medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_medal "Olympic medal")

The 2016 Olympic medals were the largest diameter of any medals presented at the Olympics up to this point. The golds were purer than any presented at all preceding Olympics. The silvers were made from recycling mirrors, solder, and X-ray plates. Just under half of the copper used in the bronze medals was recycled from normal operations at the [Brazilian Mint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_da_Moeda_do_Brasil "Casa da Moeda do Brasil"). The reverse of the medals features [Nike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nike_(mythology) "Nike (mythology)"), the Greek goddess of victory.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-32)

The medal table is based on information provided by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [Olympic medal table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_medal_table "Olympic medal table") sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-33)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-34) If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [IOC country code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_IOC_country_codes "List of IOC country codes").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-35)

Events in [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Boxing at the 2016 Summer Olympics") result in a bronze medal being awarded to each of the two competitors who lose their semi-final matches, as opposed to them fighting in a [third place tie breaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_place_playoff "Third place playoff").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-36) Other combat sports, which include, [judo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judo_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Judo at the 2016 Summer Olympics"), [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Taekwondo at the 2016 Summer Olympics"), and [wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Wrestling at the 2016 Summer Olympics"), use a [repechage system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repechage_system "Repechage system") which also results in two bronze medals being awarded.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-37)

Two gold medals and no silver medals were awarded due to a first-place tie in the [women's 100 metre freestyle swimming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre freestyle") event,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-38) while three silver medals and no bronze medals were awarded due to a second-place tie in the [men's 100 metre butterfly swimming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_100_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metre butterfly") event.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-39) Additionally, two bronze medals were awarded for a third-place tie in the [women's 100 metre backstroke swimming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_backstroke "Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre backstroke") and in the [men's K-1 200 metres canoeing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canoeing_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_K-1_200_metres "Canoeing at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's K-1 200 metres") events.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-40)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-41)

[Nijat Rahimov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nijat_Rahimov "Nijat Rahimov") of Kazakhstan originally won the gold medal in [men's 77 kg weightlifting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weightlifting_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_77_kg "Weightlifting at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's 77 kg") but was disqualified in March 2022 by the [Court of Arbitration for Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Arbitration_for_Sport "Court of Arbitration for Sport") (CAS) for doping violations.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-42)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-43) As of July 2024, the medals have not yet been re-allocated and will not be until final rulings by the IOC have been issued.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-77kg_medal_redistro-44)

The [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics"), officially known as the Games of the XXXI Olympiad, and officially branded as Rio 2016, were an international [multi-sport event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-sport_event "Multi-sport event") held from 5 to 21 August 2016 in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), Brazil, with preliminary events in some sports beginning on 3 August.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-IOC_Rio_2016-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-4) 11,238 athletes representing 207 [National Olympic Committees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") (NOCs) participated, including first-time entrants [Kosovo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kosovo_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Kosovo at the 2016 Summer Olympics"), [South Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "South Sudan at the 2016 Summer Olympics"), and the [Refugee Olympic Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugee_Olympic_Team_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Refugee Olympic Team at the 2016 Summer Olympics").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-IOC_Rio_2016-3) The games featured 306 medal events in 28 [sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_sports "Olympic sports") and 41 disciplines.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-IOC_Rio_2016-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-5) The 2016 Summer Games were the first Olympics to be held in [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-6)

Athletes representing 87 NOCs received at least one medal, breaking the record of most NOCs winning a medal at a single edition of the Olympics.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-7)[[A]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-12) Athletes from 59 nations The [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "United States at the 2016 Summer Olympics") led the medal table both in number of gold medals won and in overall medals, winning 46 and 121 respectively.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-27) American swimmer [Michael Phelps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Phelps "Michael Phelps") won the most gold medals at the games with five and the most total medals with six (five gold, one silver).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-28) This marked the fourth consecutive [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games") in which Phelps led all athletes in gold and total medals.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-29)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-30)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-31)

## Medals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Medals")]

See also: [Olympic medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_medal "Olympic medal")

The 2016 Olympic medals were the largest diameter of any medals presented at the Olympics up to this point. The golds were purer than any presented at all preceding Olympics. The silvers were made from recycling mirrors, solder, and X-ray plates. Just under half of the copper used in the bronze medals was recycled from normal operations at the [Brazilian Mint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_da_Moeda_do_Brasil "Casa da Moeda do Brasil"). The reverse of the medals features [Nike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nike_(mythology) "Nike (mythology)"), the Greek goddess of victory.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-32)

The medal table is based on information provided by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [Olympic medal table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_medal_table "Olympic medal table") sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-33)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-34) If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [IOC country code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_IOC_country_codes "List of IOC country codes").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-35)

Events in [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Boxing at the 2016 Summer Olympics") result in a bronze medal being awarded to each of the two competitors who lose their semi-final matches, as opposed to them fighting in a [third place tie breaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_place_playoff "Third place playoff").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-36) Other combat sports, which include, [judo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judo_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Judo at the 2016 Summer Olympics"), [taekwondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taekwondo_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Taekwondo at the 2016 Summer Olympics"), and [wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Wrestling at the 2016 Summer Olympics"), use a [repechage system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repechage_system "Repechage system") which also results in two bronze medals being awarded.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-37)

Two gold medals and no silver medals were awarded due to a first-place tie in the [women's 100 metre freestyle swimming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_freestyle "Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre freestyle") event,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-38) while three silver medals and no bronze medals were awarded due to a second-place tie in the [men's 100 metre butterfly swimming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_100_metre_butterfly "Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metre butterfly") event.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-39) Additionally, two bronze medals were awarded for a third-place tie in the [women's 100 metre backstroke swimming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_100_metre_backstroke "Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metre backstroke") and in the [men's K-1 200 metres canoeing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canoeing_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_K-1_200_metres "Canoeing at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's K-1 200 metres") events.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-40)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-41)

[Nijat Rahimov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nijat_Rahimov "Nijat Rahimov") of Kazakhstan originally won the gold medal in [men's 77 kg weightlifting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weightlifting_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_77_kg "Weightlifting at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's 77 kg") but was disqualified in March 2022 by the [Court of Arbitration for Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Arbitration_for_Sport "Court of Arbitration for Sport") (CAS) for doping violations.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-42)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-43) As of July 2024, the medals have not yet been re-allocated and will not be until final rulings by the IOC have been issued.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-77kg_medal_redistro-44)

2.   ↑[Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrain_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Bahrain at the 2012 Summer Olympics") was retroactively awarded a gold medal in 2021 for the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") due to a medal reallocation of the [women's 1500 metres race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_1500_metres "Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's 1500 metres"). [Maryam Yusuf Jamal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryam_Yusuf_Jamal "Maryam Yusuf Jamal") had originally finished third.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-16)

4.   ↑The [Independent Olympic Athletes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Olympic_Athletes_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Independent Olympic Athletes at the 2016 Summer Olympics") team was composed of nine [Kuwaiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuwait_at_the_Olympics "Kuwait at the Olympics") athletes competing under the Olympic flag, as the [Kuwait Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuwait_Olympic_Committee "Kuwait Olympic Committee") had been suspended by the IOC due to political interference.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-47)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-48)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-49) While the [Refugee Olympic Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugee_Olympic_Team_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Refugee Olympic Team at the 2016 Summer Olympics") also competed under the Olympic flag, they were not considered independent.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#cite_note-50)

The [United States of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") has sent [athletes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athlete "Athlete") to every celebration of the modern [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") with the exception of the [1980 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics "1980 Summer Olympics"), during which it led a [boycott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics_boycott "1980 Summer Olympics boycott") in protest of the [Soviet Union's invasion of Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet%E2%80%93Afghan_War "Soviet–Afghan War"). The [United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Olympic_&_Paralympic_Committee "United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee") (USOPC) is the [National Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") for the United States.

American athletes have won a total of 2,774 medals (1,106 of them gold) at the [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games"), and another 363 (126 of them gold) at the [Winter Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_Olympic_Games "Winter Olympic Games"), making the United States the most prolific medal-winning nation in the history of the Olympics. The U.S. has placed first in the Summer Olympic medal table [19 times out of 30 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_teams_by_medals_won#List_by_team "List of Olympic teams by medals won") and 29 appearances (having boycotted in 1980), but has had less success in the Winter Olympics, placing first [once in 24 participations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_teams_by_medals_won#List_by_team_2 "List of Olympic teams by medals won").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-1) The United States have been the host nation for the modern Olympics on eight occasions so far.

The United States Olympic contingent is the only Olympic contingent in the world to receive no government funding; neither training and development costs nor prize money are provided by the U.S. national government.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-:0-4)

## Hosted Games

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=United_States_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Hosted Games")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Phelps_carries_Stars_%26_Stripes_%2828726351981%29.jpg/500px-Phelps_carries_Stars_%26_Stripes_%2828726351981%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Phelps_carries_Stars_&_Stripes_(28726351981).jpg)

[Michael Phelps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Phelps "Michael Phelps")[carrying the flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_flag_bearers_for_the_United_States_at_the_Olympics "List of flag bearers for the United States at the Olympics") on behalf of athletes from the United States during the [parade of nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_Parade_of_Nations "2016 Summer Olympics Parade of Nations") at the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics"). With 28 Olympic medals (23 of them gold), he is the most decorated Olympian of all time.

The United States has hosted the modern Olympic Games eight times, more than any other nation. These occasions span from the 1904 St. Louis Olympics to the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Olympics. Beyond hosting, the U.S. has significantly impacted the Olympics through athletic achievements, innovations in sports infrastructure and technology, and cultural contributions. Its influence extends to advocating Olympic ideals and leaving lasting legacies in host cities. Overall, the U.S. plays a central role in the history and ongoing development of the Olympic movement. For example, the 1932 Los Angeles Olympics pioneered the use of electronic timing devices. The 1984 Los Angeles Olympics set new standards for opening and closing ceremonies, as well as being the first privately financed and commercially successful games in history. Hosting the Olympics has also left lasting legacies in host cities, such as improved infrastructure, economic benefits, and increased tourism. For example, the 1996 Atlanta Olympics revitalized parts of the city and left behind sporting venues still in use today.

In 2028, the third Los Angeles Olympics will mark the ninth occasion that the Olympics are hosted in the U.S.

## Medal tables

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=United_States_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Medal tables")]

See also: [All-time Olympic Games medal table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-time_Olympic_Games_medal_table "All-time Olympic Games medal table")

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Francis_Field_1904.jpg/250px-Francis_Field_1904.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Francis_Field_1904.jpg)

[Francis Olympic Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Olympic_Field "Francis Olympic Field") of [Washington University in St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_University_in_St._Louis "Washington University in St. Louis"), site of the [1904 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_Summer_Olympics "1904 Summer Olympics"). The 1904 Summer Olympics in St. Louis, Missouri were the first Olympic Games held outside of Europe.

The United States made its Olympic debut in 1896 in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens"), the very first [edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_Summer_Olympics "1896 Summer Olympics") of the modern games. The nation performed inconsistently in the pre-[World War-I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") period, primarily due to fielding considerably fewer athletes than host countries, with the exception being the [1904 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_Summer_Olympics "1904 Summer Olympics") in [St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis "St. Louis"), [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"), where the U.S. achieved its largest medal haul in history, a record that still stands today. During the [interwar period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interwar_period "Interwar period"), the U.S. enjoyed its greatest success, topping both gold and total medal counts at four straight Summer Games, before falling short in the [1936 Berlin games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_Summer_Olympics "1936 Summer Olympics"). The next summer Olympics were held in [1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Summer_Olympics "1948 Summer Olympics") following [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"). In [1952](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_Summer_Olympics "1952 Summer Olympics"), the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union_at_the_Olympics "Soviet Union at the Olympics") made its Olympic debut, initiating a state-sponsored approach to international sport focused on projecting socio-political superiority. The rapid rise of the Soviet Union to challenge the United States as a leading Olympic power raised questions and suspicion about the means used to achieve this, including the pretense of professional athletes having amateur status and allegations of state-sponsored doping. After 20 years of competition on the Olympic stage, the USSR convincingly topped the gold medal chart at the [1972 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics "1972 Summer Olympics") in [Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich"). After that, the U.S. would not top the medal table in non-boycotted games until the [1996 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics"), five years after the USSR [collapsed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Soviet_Union "Fall of the Soviet Union").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-A_Real_Pro-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-7) A bright spot for the United States was the [1984 games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Olympics "1984 Summer Olympics") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), where the U.S. set a record for most gold medals won in a single Olympics (83), buoyed by the [Soviet-led boycott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Olympics_boycott "1984 Summer Olympics boycott"). Coincident with a drive by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") toward gender parity beginning in the 1990s, the U.S.'s fortunes improved, and the nation topped the medal table in the Summer Olympics six times since 1992 and placed second on two occasions.

In contrast to its summer Olympics status, the United States was not a power in the Winter Games until the [2002 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Winter_Olympics "2002 Winter Olympics") in [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City"). Hosting the games in 2002 boosted the U.S. winter sports program; since then, the country's athletes have performed consistently well, never placing below fourth in the medal count. The nation won the most medals (37) at the [2010 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Winter_Olympics "2010 Winter Olympics") in [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver") but dropped to 23 medals at the [2018 games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Winter_Olympics "2018 Winter Olympics") in [Pyeongchang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyeongchang "Pyeongchang").

*   **NAT**Athletes at the early Olympic Games (1896, 1900, and 1904) are attributed by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) according to the national affiliation of their club or team, rather than their [nationality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationality "Nationality").[[nb 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-nationality-12)
    *   **1900 Olympic Games:**  
Canadian [George Orton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Orton "George Orton")([CAN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Canada at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) won a gold medal and a bronze medal in athletics; as a representative of an American club, his results were attributed to the United States. Conversely, American [Pauline Whittier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_Whittier "Pauline Whittier") (silver in golf) represented a Swiss club, while [Abbie Pratt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbie_Pratt "Abbie Pratt") (bronze in golf) represented a French club; their medals were therefore attributed to [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "Switzerland at the 1900 Summer Olympics") and [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "France at the 1900 Summer Olympics"), respectively. 
    *   **1904 Olympic Games:**  
Austrian [Julius Lenhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Lenhart "Julius Lenhart")([AUT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Austria at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (gymnastics; one gold and one silver), Norwegians [Bernhoff Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernhoff_Hansen "Bernhoff Hansen")([NOR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Norway at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) and [Charles Ericksen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Ericksen "Charles Ericksen")([NOR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Norway at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (wrestling; one gold each), Frenchman [Albert Corey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Corey "Albert Corey")([FRA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "France at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (athletics; one silver), Australian [Francis Gailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Gailey "Francis Gailey")([AUS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Australia at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (swimming; three silver and one bronze), German [Frank Kugler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Kugler "Frank Kugler")([GER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Germany at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (wrestling and weightlifting; one silver and two bronze), Austrian [Otto Wahle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otto_Wahle "Otto Wahle")([AUT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Austria at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (swimming; one bronze), and Swiss [Gustav Tiefenthaler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustav_Tiefenthaler "Gustav Tiefenthaler")([SUI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Switzerland at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (wrestling; one bronze) represented American clubs, and their results were attributed to the United States.

*   **MIX**At the 1904 Summer Olympics [three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#Team_events "1904 Summer Olympics medal table") team event medals (1 gold, 1 silver, and 1 bronze) won by American clubs competing as [mixed teams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_teams_at_the_Olympics "Mixed teams at the Olympics")—composed primarily of American athletes alongside a few non-American participants—were attributed to the United States: gold in the [gymnastics team all-around](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_team "Gymnastics at the 1904 Summer Olympics – Men's team"), silver in the [4 mile team race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_4_miles_team_race "Athletics at the 1904 Summer Olympics – Men's 4 miles team race"), and bronze in the [tug of war team competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tug_of_war_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Tug of war at the 1904 Summer Olympics").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-13)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-14)

See also: [1900 Summer Olympics medal table §Changes in medal standings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#Changes_in_medal_standings "1900 Summer Olympics medal table"), and [1904 Summer Olympics medal table §Changes in medal standings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#Changes_in_medal_standings "1904 Summer Olympics medal table")

The nationalities of several medalists were disputed, as many athletes competing for American clubs or teams were recent immigrants who had not yet acquired [U.S. citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._citizenship "U.S. citizenship"). Following recommendations by Olympic historian [Bill Mallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Mallon "Bill Mallon"), the IOC adjusted its database in July 2021, attributing results by athletes [nationality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationality "Nationality"), and, from 2024 onward, attributed participation and medals according to the national affiliation of the club or team for which the athletes competed.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-16)

As of the IOC's 2024 revision, the following cases comprise for the [1900 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_Summer_Olympics "1900 Summer Olympics") a total of two medals (one gold, and one silver), and for the [1904 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_Summer_Olympics "1904 Summer Olympics") a total of 17 medals (4 gold, 7 silver, and 6 bronze) attributed to the United States, despite having been won by non-American athletes, as they represented clubs affiliated with the United States. Three of the 17 medals (1 gold, 1 silver, and 1 bronze) were won by mixed teams consisting of American clubs or teams that included non-American athletes.

Only the medals of two American athletes in the [women's individual golf event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_individual "Golf at the 1900 Summer Olympics – Women's individual") at the 1900 Games have been attributed to a foreign country. American [Pauline Whittier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_Whittier "Pauline Whittier") (silver) was affiliated with the St. Moritz Golf Club in Switzerland, while [Abbie Pratt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbie_Pratt "Abbie Pratt") (bronze) was affiliated with the Dinard Golf Club in France; their medals were therefore attributed to [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "Switzerland at the 1900 Summer Olympics") and [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "France at the 1900 Summer Olympics"), respectively.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-golf1900_pre2024-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-golf1900-18)

The [United States of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") has sent [athletes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athlete "Athlete") to every celebration of the modern [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") with the exception of the [1980 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics "1980 Summer Olympics"), during which it led a [boycott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics_boycott "1980 Summer Olympics boycott") in protest of the [Soviet Union's invasion of Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet%E2%80%93Afghan_War "Soviet–Afghan War"). The [United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Olympic_&_Paralympic_Committee "United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee") (USOPC) is the [National Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") for the United States.

American athletes have won a total of 2,774 medals (1,106 of them gold) at the [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games"), and another 363 (126 of them gold) at the [Winter Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_Olympic_Games "Winter Olympic Games"), making the United States the most prolific medal-winning nation in the history of the Olympics. The U.S. has placed first in the Summer Olympic medal table [19 times out of 30 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_teams_by_medals_won#List_by_team "List of Olympic teams by medals won") and 29 appearances (having boycotted in 1980), but has had less success in the Winter Olympics, placing first [once in 24 participations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_teams_by_medals_won#List_by_team_2 "List of Olympic teams by medals won").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-1) The United States have been the host nation for the modern Olympics on eight occasions so far.

The United States Olympic contingent is the only Olympic contingent in the world to receive no government funding; neither training and development costs nor prize money are provided by the U.S. national government.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-:0-4)

## Hosted Games

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=United_States_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Hosted Games")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Phelps_carries_Stars_%26_Stripes_%2828726351981%29.jpg/500px-Phelps_carries_Stars_%26_Stripes_%2828726351981%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Phelps_carries_Stars_&_Stripes_(28726351981).jpg)

[Michael Phelps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Phelps "Michael Phelps")[carrying the flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_flag_bearers_for_the_United_States_at_the_Olympics "List of flag bearers for the United States at the Olympics") on behalf of athletes from the United States during the [parade of nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics_Parade_of_Nations "2016 Summer Olympics Parade of Nations") at the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics"). With 28 Olympic medals (23 of them gold), he is the most decorated Olympian of all time.

The United States has hosted the modern Olympic Games eight times, more than any other nation. These occasions span from the 1904 St. Louis Olympics to the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Olympics. Beyond hosting, the U.S. has significantly impacted the Olympics through athletic achievements, innovations in sports infrastructure and technology, and cultural contributions. Its influence extends to advocating Olympic ideals and leaving lasting legacies in host cities. Overall, the U.S. plays a central role in the history and ongoing development of the Olympic movement. For example, the 1932 Los Angeles Olympics pioneered the use of electronic timing devices. The 1984 Los Angeles Olympics set new standards for opening and closing ceremonies, as well as being the first privately financed and commercially successful games in history. Hosting the Olympics has also left lasting legacies in host cities, such as improved infrastructure, economic benefits, and increased tourism. For example, the 1996 Atlanta Olympics revitalized parts of the city and left behind sporting venues still in use today.

In 2028, the third Los Angeles Olympics will mark the ninth occasion that the Olympics are hosted in the U.S.

## Medal tables

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=United_States_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Medal tables")]

See also: [All-time Olympic Games medal table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-time_Olympic_Games_medal_table "All-time Olympic Games medal table")

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Francis_Field_1904.jpg/250px-Francis_Field_1904.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Francis_Field_1904.jpg)

[Francis Olympic Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Olympic_Field "Francis Olympic Field") of [Washington University in St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_University_in_St._Louis "Washington University in St. Louis"), site of the [1904 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_Summer_Olympics "1904 Summer Olympics"). The 1904 Summer Olympics in St. Louis, Missouri were the first Olympic Games held outside of Europe.

The United States made its Olympic debut in 1896 in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens"), the very first [edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_Summer_Olympics "1896 Summer Olympics") of the modern games. The nation performed inconsistently in the pre-[World War-I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") period, primarily due to fielding considerably fewer athletes than host countries, with the exception being the [1904 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_Summer_Olympics "1904 Summer Olympics") in [St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis "St. Louis"), [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"), where the U.S. achieved its largest medal haul in history, a record that still stands today. During the [interwar period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interwar_period "Interwar period"), the U.S. enjoyed its greatest success, topping both gold and total medal counts at four straight Summer Games, before falling short in the [1936 Berlin games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_Summer_Olympics "1936 Summer Olympics"). The next summer Olympics were held in [1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Summer_Olympics "1948 Summer Olympics") following [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"). In [1952](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_Summer_Olympics "1952 Summer Olympics"), the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union_at_the_Olympics "Soviet Union at the Olympics") made its Olympic debut, initiating a state-sponsored approach to international sport focused on projecting socio-political superiority. The rapid rise of the Soviet Union to challenge the United States as a leading Olympic power raised questions and suspicion about the means used to achieve this, including the pretense of professional athletes having amateur status and allegations of state-sponsored doping. After 20 years of competition on the Olympic stage, the USSR convincingly topped the gold medal chart at the [1972 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics "1972 Summer Olympics") in [Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich"). After that, the U.S. would not top the medal table in non-boycotted games until the [1996 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics"), five years after the USSR [collapsed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Soviet_Union "Fall of the Soviet Union").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-A_Real_Pro-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-7) A bright spot for the United States was the [1984 games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Olympics "1984 Summer Olympics") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), where the U.S. set a record for most gold medals won in a single Olympics (83), buoyed by the [Soviet-led boycott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Olympics_boycott "1984 Summer Olympics boycott"). Coincident with a drive by the [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") toward gender parity beginning in the 1990s, the U.S.'s fortunes improved, and the nation topped the medal table in the Summer Olympics six times since 1992 and placed second on two occasions.

In contrast to its summer Olympics status, the United States was not a power in the Winter Games until the [2002 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Winter_Olympics "2002 Winter Olympics") in [Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City"). Hosting the games in 2002 boosted the U.S. winter sports program; since then, the country's athletes have performed consistently well, never placing below fourth in the medal count. The nation won the most medals (37) at the [2010 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Winter_Olympics "2010 Winter Olympics") in [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver") but dropped to 23 medals at the [2018 games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Winter_Olympics "2018 Winter Olympics") in [Pyeongchang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyeongchang "Pyeongchang").

Conversely, American [Pauline Whittier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_Whittier "Pauline Whittier") (silver in golf) represented a Swiss club, while [Abbie Pratt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbie_Pratt "Abbie Pratt") (bronze in golf) represented a French club; their medals were therefore attributed to [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "Switzerland at the 1900 Summer Olympics") and [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_at_the_1900_Summer_Olympics "France at the 1900 Summer Olympics"), respectively. 
    *   **1904 Olympic Games:**  
Austrian [Julius Lenhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Lenhart "Julius Lenhart")([AUT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Austria at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (gymnastics; one gold and one silver), Norwegians [Bernhoff Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernhoff_Hansen "Bernhoff Hansen")([NOR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Norway at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) and [Charles Ericksen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Ericksen "Charles Ericksen")([NOR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Norway at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (wrestling; one gold each), Frenchman [Albert Corey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Corey "Albert Corey")([FRA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "France at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (athletics; one silver), Australian [Francis Gailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Gailey "Francis Gailey")([AUS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Australia at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (swimming; three silver and one bronze), German [Frank Kugler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Kugler "Frank Kugler")([GER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Germany at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (wrestling and weightlifting; one silver and two bronze), Austrian [Otto Wahle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otto_Wahle "Otto Wahle")([AUT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Austria at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (swimming; one bronze), and Swiss [Gustav Tiefenthaler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustav_Tiefenthaler "Gustav Tiefenthaler")([SUI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Switzerland at the 1904 Summer Olympics")) (wrestling; one bronze) represented American clubs, and their results were attributed to the United States.

*   **MIX**At the 1904 Summer Olympics [three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#Team_events "1904 Summer Olympics medal table") team event medals (1 gold, 1 silver, and 1 bronze) won by American clubs competing as [mixed teams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_teams_at_the_Olympics "Mixed teams at the Olympics")—composed primarily of American athletes alongside a few non-American participants—were attributed to the United States: gold in the [gymnastics team all-around](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_team "Gymnastics at the 1904 Summer Olympics – Men's team"), silver in the [4 mile team race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_4_miles_team_race "Athletics at the 1904 Summer Olympics – Men's 4 miles team race"), and bronze in the [tug of war team competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tug_of_war_at_the_1904_Summer_Olympics "Tug of war at the 1904 Summer Olympics").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-13)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-14)

### Reallocated medals of the 1900 and 1904 Summer Olympics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=United_States_at_the_Olympics&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Reallocated medals of the 1900 and 1904 Summer Olympics")]

See also: [1900 Summer Olympics medal table §Changes in medal standings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#Changes_in_medal_standings "1900 Summer Olympics medal table"), and [1904 Summer Olympics medal table §Changes in medal standings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_Summer_Olympics_medal_table#Changes_in_medal_standings "1904 Summer Olympics medal table")

The nationalities of several medalists were disputed, as many athletes competing for American clubs or teams were recent immigrants who had not yet acquired [U.S. citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._citizenship "U.S. citizenship"). Following recommendations by Olympic historian [Bill Mallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Mallon "Bill Mallon"), the IOC adjusted its database in July 2021, attributing results by athletes [nationality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationality "Nationality"), and, from 2024 onward, attributed participation and medals according to the national affiliation of the club or team for which the athletes competed.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_at_the_Olympics#cite_note-16)

As of the IOC's 2024 revision, the following cases comprise for the [1900 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_Summer_Olympics "1900 Summer Olympics") a total of two medals (one gold, and one silver), and for the [1904 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1904_Summer_Olympics "1904 Summer Olympics") a total of 17 medals (4 gold, 7 silver, and 6 bronze) attributed to the United States, despite having been won by non-American athletes, as they represented clubs affiliated with the United States. Athleticsedit
Main article: Athletics at the 1924 Summer Olympics

Ninety-six athletes represented the United States in 1924. It was the nation's seventh appearance in the sport. The United States was one of three nations, along with Great Britain and Greece, to have competed in each edition of the Olympic athletics program to that point. The American team had competitors in each of the 27 events, with the maximum number of entries in all but 3 of them (the United States did not send full teams for the steeplechase, the racewalk, or the triple jump). The United States had finalists in every event except the triple jump. The team swept the medals in two events: the pole vault and the shot put.

The United States won 32 medals overall, almost twice that of the next most successful nation (Finland). The 12 gold medals won by the Americans were two more than Finland won, putting the United States at the top of the leaderboard for the sport. Houser and Osborn were the most successful individuals, with two gold medals apiece. Earl Johnson and Scholz won two medals each. Thirty-three other athletes won medals, bringing the total to 37 of 96 participants taking medals.

Boxingedit
Main article: Boxing at the 1924 Summer Olympics

Sixteen boxers represented the United States at the 1924 Games; the U.S. was one of four countries (along with France, Great Britain, and Italy) to send two boxers in each weight class. It was the nation's third appearance in the sport. The two gold medals won by Americans matched Britain's pair of golds. The United States team won the most overall medals with six.

In two weight classes, both American boxers won medals. The featherweight final featured two Americans, with Fields coming out on top. LaBarba won the flyweight, with Fee taking the bronze in that weight class. All six medals came in the lightest four weight classes, with Tripoli's silver in the bantamweight and Boylstein's bronze in the lightweight rounding out the total.

Divingedit
Main article: Diving at the 1924 Summer Olympics

Ten divers, five men and five women, represented the United States in 1924. It was the nation's fifth appearance in the sport; the United States was the only nation to have appeared at each Olympic diving competition to that point. The Americans were dominant, sweeping the medals in three of the five events and taking the top two places in a fourth. The United States entered three divers in each event for a total of 15 entries; 11 resulted in medals while all 15 advanced to the finals. White was the top individual diver, with gold medals in both of his events. Becker won a gold and a silver. Smith took a gold, while Pinkston took a pair of bronzes. Riggin, Fall, and Desjardins each won a silver, and Fletcher took a bronze. Thrash and Meany were the only two Americans to not win medals.

Equestrianedit
Main article: Equestrian at the 1924 Summer Olympics

Five equestrians represented the United States in 1924. It was the nation's fourth appearance in the sport; the United States was the only nation to have taken part in each Olympic equestrian competition to date. Doak won the individual eventing bronze, the United States's first medal since 1912 and matching their all-time best result in the sport. Doak and Carr, who finished eighth in the eventing, gave the United States a strong shot at silver in the team competition, but neither Barry nor Padgett finished and so the team did not get a score. Padgett, this time along with Bontecou, again did not finish in the show jumping competition, and the United States did not get a score in that competition either. Barry's 25th place was the best individual result in show jumping.

Main article: Polo at the 1924 Summer Olympics

The United States sent a polo team to the Olympics for the third time in 1924. The Americans won their first three games, against the three European sides, and faced Argentina in their final game. Despite having a late lead, the United States was unable to finish off the Argentinians, who came from behind to beat the United States. The United States finished with the silver medal.

Rugby unionedit
Main article: Rugby union at the 1924 Summer Olympics

The United States sent a rugby team to the Olympics for the second time in 1924. The defending champions won their first game against Romania, 37 to 0. As France had already beaten Romania, the three-team round-robin finished with the France-United States match. The Americans won 17 to 3 to become the first team to successfully defend an Olympic rugby championship.

Athleticsedit
Main article: Athletics at the 1924 Summer Olympics

Ninety-six athletes represented the United States in 1924. It was the nation's seventh appearance in the sport. The United States was one of three nations, along with Great Britain and Greece, to have competed in each edition of the Olympic athletics program to that point. The American team had competitors in each of the 27 events, with the maximum number of entries in all but 3 of them (the United States did not send full teams for the steeplechase, the racewalk, or the triple jump). The United States had finalists in every event except the triple jump. The team swept the medals in two events: the pole vault and the shot put.

The United States won 32 medals overall, almost twice that of the next most successful nation (Finland). The 12 gold medals won by the Americans were two more than Finland won, putting the United States at the top of the leaderboard for the sport. Houser and Osborn were the most successful individuals, with two gold medals apiece. Earl Johnson and Scholz won two medals each. Thirty-three other athletes won medals, bringing the total to 37 of 96 participants taking medals.

Boxingedit
Main article: Boxing at the 1924 Summer Olympics

Sixteen boxers represented the United States at the 1924 Games; the U.S. was one of four countries (along with France, Great Britain, and Italy) to send two boxers in each weight class. It was the nation's third appearance in the sport. The two gold medals won by Americans matched Britain's pair of golds. The United States team won the most overall medals with six.

In two weight classes, both American boxers won medals. The featherweight final featured two Americans, with Fields coming out on top. LaBarba won the flyweight, with Fee taking the bronze in that weight class. All six medals came in the lightest four weight classes, with Tripoli's silver in the bantamweight and Boylstein's bronze in the lightweight rounding out the total.

Divingedit
Main article: Diving at the 1924 Summer Olympics

Ten divers, five men and five women, represented the United States in 1924. It was the nation's fifth appearance in the sport; the United States was the only nation to have appeared at each Olympic diving competition to that point. The Americans were dominant, sweeping the medals in three of the five events and taking the top two places in a fourth. The United States entered three divers in each event for a total of 15 entries; 11 resulted in medals while all 15 advanced to the finals. White was the top individual diver, with gold medals in both of his events. Becker won a gold and a silver. Smith took a gold, while Pinkston took a pair of bronzes. Riggin, Fall, and Desjardins each won a silver, and Fletcher took a bronze. Thrash and Meany were the only two Americans to not win medals.

Equestrianedit
Main article: Equestrian at the 1924 Summer Olympics

Five equestrians represented the United States in 1924. It was the nation's fourth appearance in the sport; the United States was the only nation to have taken part in each Olympic equestrian competition to date. Doak won the individual eventing bronze, the United States's first medal since 1912 and matching their all-time best result in the sport. Doak and Carr, who finished eighth in the eventing, gave the United States a strong shot at silver in the team competition, but neither Barry nor Padgett finished and so the team did not get a score. Padgett, this time along with Bontecou, again did not finish in the show jumping competition, and the United States did not get a score in that competition either. Barry's 25th place was the best individual result in show jumping.

Poloedit
Main article: Polo at the 1924 Summer Olympics

The United States sent a polo team to the Olympics for the third time in 1924. The Americans won their first three games, against the three European sides, and faced Argentina in their final game. Despite having a late lead, the United States was unable to finish off the Argentinians, who came from behind to beat the United States. The United States finished with the silver medal.

Rugby unionedit
Main article: Rugby union at the 1924 Summer Olympics

The United States sent a rugby team to the Olympics for the second time in 1924. The defending champions won their first game against Romania, 37 to 0. As France had already beaten Romania, the three-team round-robin finished with the France-United States match. The Americans won 17 to 3 to become the first team to successfully defend an Olympic rugby championship.

Canada has competed at 27 [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games"), missing only the inaugural [1896 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_Summer_Olympics "1896 Summer Olympics") and the boycotted [1980 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics "1980 Summer Olympics"). This count includes the [1906 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1906_Intercalated_Games "1906 Intercalated Games"), deemed unofficial 43 years after they were held (Canada won a gold and silver medal). The nation made its debut at the [1900 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_Summer_Olympics "1900 Summer Olympics"). Canada competes under the [IOC country code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_IOC_country_codes "List of IOC country codes") CAN.

## Hosted games

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Canada_at_the_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Hosted games")]

Canada has hosted the [Summer Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games") once, in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Summer_Olympics "1976 Summer Olympics") in [Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal "Montreal"), [Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec "Quebec").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_at_the_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-r262-1)
